tropes.html: Horace and Jasper try this as electric repairmen. It doesn't fool the nanny, so they just barge their way in. It doesn't help that Horace says they're from the gas company.

tropes.name: Jerk with a Heart of Gold
tropes.html: Patch is established as the most aggressive of the 15 puppies, relatively speaking. He trash-talks Thunderbolt's human rival and angrily barks at Horace for bullying Lucky. When the puppies reunite with their parents, Patch is the first to say that they need to take care of the other 84 puppies.

tropes.name: Jump Scare
tropes.html:
• Roger and Pongo get one from Nanny of all people when she announces that THE PUPPIES ARE HERE!!!
  • Then there's the bandit Thunderbolt is fighting on the television, scaring the daylights out of Lucky who stood too close for his own good.

tropes.name: Just in Time
tropes.html: The moment when the Baduns have cornered Sgt. Tibbs and the puppies and are about to kill them, Pongo and Perdita smash through a window and attack the would-be murderers.

tropes.name: Kidnapped While Sleeping
tropes.html: Horace and Jasper Badun abduct Pongo and Perdita's 15 puppies just after Nanny has put them to bed.

tropes.name: Know-Nothing Know-It-All
tropes.html: Jasper's shtick with Horace is that Horace hits upon what's really going on and then Jasper emphatically calls him an idiot for getting such a stupid idea.

tropes.name: Laughably Evil
tropes.html: As ruthless as Cruella and her goons are in stealing (and attempted murder of) the puppies, their overblown whimsy and bumbling make up a lot of the movie's humor. It helps that Roger starts singing "The Villain Sucks" Song and then starts playing it in the attic as background noise when Cruella first appears onscreen.

tropes.name: Light Is Not Good
tropes.html: Cruella's fur coat is light-colored, yet she is the villain.

tropes.name: Lightning Reveal
tropes.html: After Roger saves the fifteenth puppy from death, lighting crashes and everyone turns to the door to see Cruella standing in the doorframe.

tropes.name: Limited Animation
tropes.html: While still a literal film when compared to most theatrical cartoons from the time, most of the character designs and backgrounds have an abstract stylized look inspired by the works of UPA. The Kanine Krunchies commercial is especially animated in the limited style of animated commercials of the sixties.

tropes.name: Literal Ass-Kicking
tropes.html: Horace and Jasper get kicked in the behind by Captain the horse — hard enough for their heads to break through the wall of the barn!

tropes.name: Love at First Sight
tropes.html: Pongo instantly takes to Perdita, calling her "the most beautiful creature on four legs".

tropes.name: Making Room for Baby
tropes.html: Early in the film, Pongo and Perdita have fifteen puppies, and their human masters — Roger and Anita — are uncertain whether they will have room for all of them. Over the course of the movie, Pongo and Perdita rescue 84 more puppies from the villain. Luckily, by the time they get back to their masters, Roger has struck gold with a hit song, and he and Anita are easily persuaded to adopt all the puppies, with Roger gleefully announcing that "We'll buy a big place, in the country!" to accommodate them all. The sequel, 101 Dalmatians II: Patch's London Adventure begins with the Radcliffs moving from London to the Dalmatian Plantation farm (although Patch gets left behind).

tropes.name: Mama Bear
tropes.html: As if traveling through the English countryside in the middle of winter to save their puppies wasn't enough, Pongo and Perdita are scary when they burst in to attack Horace and Jasper, snarling with bared teeth and their eyes flashing red. Considering they just interrupted the Badduns as they were about to bludgeon their children to death, who can blame them?

tropes.name: Married Animals
tropes.html: Perdita and Pongo get married along with their owners.

tropes.name: Mass "Oh, Crap!"
tropes.html: The puppies in Hell Hall cower in fright when Cruella orders Jasper and Horace to kill them.

tropes.name: Meaningful Name
tropes.html:
• The Big Bad Cruella de Ville, given that she's indeed cruel, and her last name is a pun on "devil".
  • The Bumbling Henchmen Duo Horace and Jaspar Baddun (bad one).
  • Some of the puppies have names alluding to their personalities. Patch has an eye patch; Rolly is a roly-poly; Freckles has spots resembling Youthful Freckles; Lucky has a pattern of spots in the shape of a horseshoe. However, Lucky most likely got his name from the fact that he was revived shortly after birth.

tropes.name: Meet Cute
tropes.html: Invoked by Pongo who was probably going for more of a conventional Boy Meets Girl scenario, but his intervention leads to Roger and Anita's (and consequently his and Perdita's) first meeting starting out as this.

tropes.name: Medium Awareness
tropes.html: The Kanine Krunchies salesman on TV stops his speech to gasp in shock when Pongo turns the set off.

tropes.name: Men Can't Keep House
tropes.html: Commented on by Pongo at the beginning of the film, Roger's flat is a horror.

tropes.name: Named by the Adaptation
tropes.html: In the book, only four of the puppies are given names: Lucky, Patch, Roly Poly and Cadpig. In the movie, while dropping Cadpig (her characterization passed on to Lucky) and simplifying Roly Poly's name to just "Rolly," gives us the additional puppy names Freckles, Penny and Pepper.

tropes.name: Near-Villain Victory
tropes.html: If Horace hadn't yanked out the steering wheel of the Baduns' truck in panic, causing them to lose control and crash into Cruella, there's almost certainly no way the dalmatians would have escaped her — her car was literally hanging onto the van. That's how very, very badly Cruella wants that fur coat.

tropes.name: Newspaper-Thin Disguise
tropes.html: Jasper and Horace make their entrance this way, sitting in their truck and hiding behind their newspapers until Anita and Roger have walked by.

tropes.name: Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!
tropes.html:
• Sergeant Tibbs has the horse Captain kick Horace and Jasper into a wall... and from there, the two see the dogs' footprints in the snow. Oops. Probably couldn't be helped much, though, since the alternative was letting the pair burn the whole place down.
  • When the Dalmatians are crossing a street and hear Cruella approaching, Pongo begins to sweep away their tracks. Unfortunately, he fails to sweep them all away before Cruella arrives on the scene and Cruella discovers them anyway, which leads her to eventually finding them. Then again, Pongo did the best he could to hide them.

tropes.name: Nice Job Fixing It, Villain!
tropes.html: Jasper tries to hit Pongo with a fireplace poker, but by doing so creates a large hole in the door, which allows the Dalmatians to escape the mansion.

tropes.name: Nightmare Face
tropes.html:
• Cruella certainly has one as she's about to ram to back of the van during the climactic Chase Scene.
  • Pongo and Perdita are scary too when they get their Game Face on.

tropes.name: No One Gets Left Behind
tropes.html: Pongo and Patch refuse to leave behind the other puppies even though they certainly will not have the room at home to accommodate them all. Nonetheless, Perdita agrees without argument and adopts them all as her kids.

tropes.name: No One Should Survive That!
tropes.html: Cruella, Jasper and Horace all managed to survive their vehicles colliding and tumbling down a hill without any noticeable injuries, even though both their vehicles were completely totaled.

tropes.name: No Time to Explain
tropes.html: When Pongo and Perdita meet the Colonel, they inquire about their puppies but he hurries them along using this line.

tropes.name: Not Even Bothering with the Accent
tropes.html: None of the child actors bother attempting British accents while voicing the Dalmatian puppies, though this is averted in the direct-to-video sequel where all the puppies have the proper accents.

tropes.name: Oh, Crap!
tropes.html:
• Sergeant Tibbs' response when Jasper, mistaking him for a wine bottle, grabs him by the neck.
  • Pongo and Perdita's understandably horrified response when they learn that their puppies are being held at "the De Vil place".
  • Pongo, when water drops from ice stalactites fall on him and the puppies, exposing their Labrador disguises.
  • A more dramatic one in the climax from Pongo and Perdita, when Cruella manages to ram her car into the back of the van they're trying to escape in.
  • Cruella gets one during the climactic chase when she looks up and realizes that she's headed straight into a ravine.

tropes.name: Ominous Opera Cape
tropes.html: Cruella De Vil wears a cream fur coat with a Dracula-esque red underside.

tropes.name: Panicky Expectant Father
tropes.html: Pongo acts very anxious during the evening when his puppies are scheduled to be born. Funnily, even Roger acts anxious.

tropes.name: Papa Wolf
tropes.html: Pongo wastes no time on tracking down all of his missing puppies with Perdita by his side, and they would go on jump through a window to attack Horace and Jasper once they try to bludgeon all 99 of the puppies to death.

tropes.name: Paper Destruction of Anger
tropes.html: After Roger makes it clear to Cruella that he and Anita are not selling their puppies, Cruella angrily tears up the check she had written and throws the pieces over Roger.

tropes.name: Parental Bonus
tropes.html: At the end, when Pongo and Perdita return to the flat with their own puppies plus 84 extra, Anita asks "But where did they all come from?". Roger responds by patting Pongo on the head and saying "Pongo, you old rascal!".

tropes.name: Phony Rules
tropes.html: When Horace and Jasper enter to steal the puppies, pretending to be electricians, they claim that the house needs to be inspected by law.

tropes.name: Pie in the Face
tropes.html: Horace gets his face slammed into a cake when the piano wing collapses above him at the mansion.

tropes.name: Pink Girl, Blue Boy
tropes.html: Inverted with the dogs' collars: Pongo and the male puppies wear red collars, while Perdita and the female puppies wear blue ones. At the time the movie was made, blue was considered a feminine color and red a masculine color. Later adaptations didn't care as much. Nor did the tie-in merchandise artists.

tropes.name: Powder Gag
tropes.html: Invoked when the Dalmatians deliberately cover themselves in soot to disguise themselves as Labradors. The puppies enjoy the excuse to get dirty.

tropes.name: Pragmatic Villainy
tropes.html:
Cruella isn't happy when she finds out the police aren't dropping the case looking for the stolen 15 puppies and thus urges Jasper and Horace to get to skinning all 99 Dalmatian pups right away before they discover them hiding at Hell Hall.
Cruella: I've got no time to argue! I tell you, it's got to be done tonight! (after turning off the show Jasper and Horace were watching) Do you understand?! Tonight!
Horace: But they ain't big enough!
Jasper: You couldn't get half-a-dozen coats out of the whole kaboodle.
Cruella: Then we'll settle for half-a-dozen! We can't wait! The police are everywhere! I want the job done tonight!
Horace: 'Ow're we gonna do it?
Cruella: Anyway you like, poison them, drown them, bash them in the head! You got any chloroform?
Jasper: Not a drop.
Horace: And no ether, either (ee-ther).
Jasper: (bonks him on the head with his bottle) Either! (eye-ther)
Cruella: I don't care how you kill the little beasts, BUT DO IT! AND DO IT NOW!
Jasper: Aw, please, miss, now have pity, will ya? Can't we see the rest of the show first?
Horace: We want to see "What's My Crime?". (Cruella yanks Jasper's bottle as he takes a big swig, causing him to sputter and throws it in the fireplace where it explodes, scaring the absolute crap out of the two Baduns the puppies before giving both criminals a slap in the face)
Cruella: Now listen, you idiots! I'll be back first thing in the morning! And the job better be done or I'll— I'll— I'll call the police! DO YOU UNDERSTAND?! (slams the door hard enough some plaster from the ceiling falls on Horace's head who casually lifts it off)
Horace: (meekly) I think she means it, Jasper.

tropes.name: Pulling the Rug Out
tropes.html: Perdita takes out Horace by yanking the rug out from under him, causing him to fall into the fireplace.

tropes.name: "The Reason You Suck" Speech
tropes.html:
Cruella's unforgettable and vicious reaction to Roger flatly rejecting her offer to buy the puppies.
"Why, you horrid man! You... You... All right! Keep the little beasts for all I care! (tears up check, throws pieces over Roger) Do as you like with them! *Drown* them! But I warn you, Anita, we're through! I'm through with all of you! I'll get even! Just wait! You'll be sorry! You fools! You... YOU IDIOTS!"

tropes.name: Red and Black and Evil All Over
tropes.html: Cruella DeVil, the villain of the movie, primarily wears a white fur coat with a red underside over a black dress and red gloves. Her car is also colored red and black.

tropes.name: Red Eyes, Take Warning
tropes.html: During the climactic Chase Scene, we get two shots of Cruella with red in her eyes. The first shot comes immediately after she has driven her car out of the ditch and smashed through a tree: her irises are red. The second shot comes during her Nightmare Face moment, as she is about to ram the back of the van: her eyes are almost completely red, with her pupils star-shaped and spirals emanating from them.

tropes.name: Red Filter of Doom
tropes.html: Seen when Pongo and Perdita fight off the Baduns in the DeVil mansion.

tropes.name: Removable Steering Wheel
tropes.html: Horace and Jasper panic and tear the wheel off their truck when they're about to crash into Cruella.

tropes.name: Riddle for the Ages
tropes.html: Jasper and Horace recognize an old acquaintance of theirs, Percival "Meathead" Fauncewater, on What's My Crime?, a game show where a panel has ten guesses to figure out the unusual felony of a criminal contestant. The show runs out of time before they guess, and so the question of what the hell Meathead did remains unanswered. It's confirmed that it wasn't burglary, homicide, or violation of a public ordinance at least. There was also an earlier contestant whose crime isn't revealed, in their case because Cruella interrupted the Baduns' watching by turning off the TV so she could scold them; by the time she leaves and they turn the set back on, that first segment is over.

tropes.name: Road Rage
tropes.html: Cruella utterly loses it when she finally sees through the Labrador disguise that Pongo and company have adopted to get away from her, and proceeds to tear up the road in crazy fashion, trying to run the moving truck they're in off the road and ramming them from behind before ultimately getting t-boned by her own men.

tropes.name: Rotoscoping
tropes.html: Sort of. Cruella's car was a white model with outlines drawn on the edges shot in stop-motion in front of a white background with a high exposure; the result was then photocopied onto the cells.

tropes.name: Rump Roast
tropes.html: Occurs to Horace when he's knocked rear-first into a roaring fireplace by Perdita.

tropes.name: Sarcasm Mode
tropes.html: When Horace suggests to Jasper that the puppies have disguised themselves using soot, Jasper says, "Say now! Horace, that's just what they did. Dogs is always paintin' themselves black! (clonks Horace on the head) You idiot!"

tropes.name: Scenery Porn
tropes.html: In a retro and colorful way that perfectly complements the characters' angular designs.

tropes.name: Screen Shake
tropes.html: Happens after Horace and Jasper's Staircase Tumble comes to an end in the old house.

tropes.name: Screw the Money, I Have Rules!
tropes.html:
Cruella de Vil initially tries to just buy the fifteen puppies that Pongo and Perdita had from the Radcliffes. But Roger point-blank refuses to sell a single one to Cruella, knowing she's just going to kill them, even though he's clearly scared of what Cruella intends to do in retribution. While Cruella storms out in rage, Anita immediately praises Roger for standing up to Cruella.
Cruella: When can the puppies leave their mother? Two weeks? Three weeks?
Roger: Never.
Cruella: (standing up) What?
Roger: (stuttering) We're-We're-We're not-not s-s-selling th-the puppies. Not-Not-Not a sin-single one. Do you understand?

tropes.name: Self-Disposing Villain
tropes.html: A non-fatal example, but Cruella, Jasper and Horace are eventually defeated due to their own actions; while chasing the truck the dalmatians are in, Cruella chases the truck from behind at the same time that Jasper and Horace try to ram the truck from the side and send it down the ditch. Then Horace panics and pulls out the steering wheel, sending their car out of control and they ram Cruella's car instead, sending all three villains into the ditch with their vehicles totaled, leaving them with no way to continue the chase.

tropes.name: Share Phrase
tropes.html: One really gets the sense that the dialogue editors loved the word "idiot". note  On average, it's uttered once about every ten minutes. To help get the point across: After Horace and Jasper have stolen the puppies, Jasper is on the phone with Cruella when he says to Horace, "You idiot!" Cruella hears this insult and thinks it was meant for her, angrily hanging up in response. The exact same gag is repeated a few seconds later when Cruella calls the Radcliffes, as she hears Anita saying "You idiot!" to an angry Roger while grabbing the phone back from him. This time, however, Cruella does not immediately hang up in anger.

tropes.name: Shipper with an Agenda
tropes.html: Pongo actively works as a matchmaker for Roger and Anita, but he doesn't specifically ship them, he just wants his useless bachelor owner to get with somebody. The real ulterior motive is so he gets a chance with Anita's beautiful dalmatian, Perdita.

tropes.name: Shout-Out
tropes.html:
• During the Twilight Bark scene, various dogs from Lady and the Tramp make cameos.
  • In the first scene inside Hell Hall, the TV is showing the Silly Symphonies short Springtime.
  • What's My Crime?, a favorite TV show of the Baduns, is a pretty clear homage to What's My Line?.

tropes.name: Show Within a Show
tropes.html:
• "The Thunderbolt Adventure Hour".
  • What's My Crime?, a show mentioned in the original novel and given some more detail in the movie.

tropes.name: Shown Their Work
tropes.html: Cruella's mansion contains a suit of armor that the background artist obviously copied from a real-life Greenwich armor of the late 16th or early 17th century. Since Cruella is a Blue Blood, it's not much of a stretch to imagine that this armor has been in her family since the Elizebethan or Jacobean period.

tropes.name: Shut Up, Hannibal!
tropes.html:
When Cruella barges into the Radcliffes' flat just minutes after the puppies are born, she takes one look at Lucky — who Roger has just saved from being stillborn — and makes several nasty, catty remarks about the puppies, which angers Nanny enough to get in Cruella's face and tell her off.
Cruella: Fifteen! Fifteen puppies! How marvelous! How marvelous! How perfectly — ugh! Oh, the devil take it, they're mongrels. No spots! No spots at all! What a horrid little white rat! Ugh!
Nanny: They're not mongrels! They'll get their spots! Just wait and see!

tropes.name: Sigh of Love
tropes.html: Perdita sighs happily while she and Pongo are resting their heads on a window sill together.

tropes.name: Source Music
tropes.html: All throughout Cruella's first scene, Roger plays "The Villain Sucks" Song as loud and obnoxiously as he possibly can, utilizing a piano, a trumpet, and a trombone by turn.

tropes.name: Spanner in the Works
tropes.html: Horace grabs the steering wheel and accidentally breaks it, causes the Baduns' van to lose control and crash into Cruella's car instead of the van the Dalmatians are escaping in as was intended. This of course gives the Dalmatians a chance to escape.

tropes.name: Spoiled Sweet
tropes.html: The poodle that Pongo rejected as a potential mate. Her owner is obviously extremely wealthy, but when she hears about the missing puppies, she's as horrified as everyone else and joins in spreading the news.

tropes.name: Stylistic Suck
tropes.html: The Kanine Krunchies commercial that the puppies are watching is animated in the Limited Animation style typical for animated TV commercials of the time.

tropes.name: Surprise Inspection Ruse
tropes.html: Horace and Jasper pretend to be electric company repairmen making a surprise inspection, but Nanny won't let them in while Roger and Anita are out of the flat. Jasper then barges in, distracts Nanny by locking her in a room, and leaves once Horace has nabbed all the puppies.

tropes.name: Surprise Multiple Birth
tropes.html: Downplayed. Dogs usually have large litters, so Perdita giving birth to multiple puppies isn't a surprise to her owners. Perdita giving birth to fifteen puppies, however, is a surprise to everyone present.

tropes.name: Surrounded by Idiots
tropes.html: Like most henchmen, Jasper and Horace are nowhere near as intelligent as Cruella.

tropes.name: Technical Euphemism
tropes.html: Subverted in a Show Within a Show that Horace and Jasper are watching. A woman is trying to find a euphemism for murder and starts to say, "Do something of a violent nature", but then settles on the more casual euphemism "do someone in".

tropes.name: Tears of Defeat
tropes.html: At the climax of the film, Cruella de Vil and her henchmen give the Dalmatians chase via different vehicles. Just after Cruella rams her beat-up car against the back of the moving van the dogs are on, the Baduns accidentally drive into her and the three of them plummet into the gorge below. With the dogs now clear for escape, Cruella berates her henchmen before bursting into tears in defeat.

tropes.name: Terrible Trio
tropes.html: Cruella De Vil and her henchmen Jasper and Horace are textbook cases.

tropes.name: Thick-Line Animation
tropes.html: More so than any other Disney animated feature at the time, thanks to the use of the Xerox process giving out a more sketchy look to the animation.

tropes.name: This Cannot Be!
tropes.html: Cruella delivers this line when she discovers that the Dalmatians have disguised themselves as black Labradors.

tropes.name: This Is My Human
tropes.html: The dogs see humans as their pets. The opening of the film uses it as part of a Bait-and-Switch gag. We're initially thinking that the man monologuing about living with his pet was the man at the piano. The narrator then clarifies that said man is his pet Roger and the narrator is indeed the dalmatian Pongo.

tropes.name: Trailers Always Spoil
tropes.html: The original theatrical trailer prominently features the climactic car chase, including showing Cruella's final defeat.

tropes.name: Tropey, Come Home
tropes.html: Pongo and Perdita's fifteen puppies are stolen by Cruella de Vil and her henchmen. So Pongo and Perdita leave home and journey from London to Suffolk, where Cruella lives, to get them back. They eventually make their way back to their owners (along with 84 other puppies that Cruella bought from pet stores) just in time for Christmas.

tropes.name: Uncatty Resemblance
tropes.html: From his window, Pongo observes the resemblance between the dogs and their owners on the street below.

tropes.name: Underground Railroad
tropes.html: The Twilight Bark networks of dogs and other animals who help the dalmatians escape Cruella.

tropes.name: Vanilla Edition
tropes.html: Among all 12 of the movies that joined the top-tier Walt Disney Signature Collection of Blu-ray/Digital HD releases before Disney+'s launch, 101 Dalmatians remains the only one with a barren Disney+ Extras page.

tropes.name: Vehicle-Based Characterization
tropes.html: Cruella's car, which takes inspiration from models such as the Mercedes-Benz 500K Cabriolet, the 1936 Alvis Speed 20 SD Drophead Coupe, and the 1931 Bugatti Type 41 Royale Weinburger Cabriolet, reflects her Rich Bitch status and is just as Lean and Mean as she is, stylized with both the windshield and headlights resembling angry eyes, the grille resembling angry teeth, and the front bumper resembling two huge bottom teeth. As the car gets destroyed, the hood is ripped off, exposing the engine which blows flames out of it, making it look like a makeshift hot rod, while at the same time as its driver is undergoing a Villainous Breakdown.

tropes.name: Vile Villain, Laughable Lackey
tropes.html: Cruella de Vil is a crazy and scary-looking Rich Bitch who wants to skin Dalmatian dogs for her new coat. Horace and Jasper are her two bumbling henchmen.

tropes.name: Villain Ball
tropes.html: Cruella would have won if she stuck with the 84 dogs she bought, but she just had to kidnap the Radcliffe puppies to prove her superiority to Roger. Even if this didn't result in Pongo and Perdita coming to their rescue, she was already under pressure from the police due to being the number one suspect in the kidnapping and was going to settle for fewer coats than if she just sat back and waited for the other 84 puppies to grow to adult size before skinning them like she intended to do originally. On the other hand, it's implied that one of the reasons she wanted them skinned as puppies is because the fur of puppies is softer than the fur of adult dogs. It's even explained in the live-action remake.

tropes.name: Villain Has a Point
tropes.html: When Anita refuses Cruella’s initial offer to buy Pongo and Perdita’s puppies, Cruella makes the reasonable argument that she and Roger wouldn’t have enough money to care for seventeen dogs, especially since Roger’s songwriting career has yet to take off. This problem is actually addressed in the ending, as Roger’s first hit song (incidentally about Cruella) earns him enough money so they can move to a bigger home for themselves and their dogs, plus the 84 new ones Pongo and Perdita adopted.

tropes.name: Villainous Breakdown
tropes.html: Cruella during the climactic Chase Scene. This is especially acute after she accidentally drives her car down a ditch and then storms back to the road at full speed, in the process smashing through a tree and turning the car into a hot rod. By now, she is plenty pissed off, and it has become clear that it's the dalmatians or her — and she doesn't care who gets in her way.

tropes.name: Villains Out Shopping
tropes.html: Jasper and Horace are watching the programme What’s My Crime? in Hell Hall when Cruella informs them she wants the puppies killed and skinned. At one point she turns the TV off because they’re more interested in watching than paying attention to her. After she storms out, they decide to finish watching the programme before getting on with the job. This allows Tibbs time to get the puppies out of the living room.

tropes.name: "The Villain Sucks" Song
tropes.html: You know the one. It probably got published either because Cruella's universally acknowledged as a horrible person, or the publishers thought it was a made-up name.

tropes.name: Watch the Paint Job
tropes.html: Cruella epicly trashes and then wrecks her own presumably-valuable classic car in her rage-induced pursuit of the puppies. It even returns in the sequel, having apparently been very cheaply slapped back together. (Guess she's not as rich as she comes across.)

tropes.name: Wham Line
tropes.html:
• Sergeant Tibbs goes to Cruella De Vil's old mansion to investigate the case of the 15 stolen Dalmatian puppies, and as he meets one puppy:
    Tibbs: Are you one of the fifteen stolen puppies?
    Dalmatian Puppy: Oh, no, we're not stolen. We're bought and paid for. There's 99 of us all together.
    Tibbs: (rubs his eyes and stares in shock) Ninety-nine?!
    (cue the Wham Shot of all these puppies, clearly more than fifteen, in the same room together)
  • Then later, we learn what Cruella plans to do with all these puppies.
    Cruella: The job has to be done tonight!
    Horace: But they ain't big enough.
    Jasper: You couldn't get half a dozen coats out of the whole caboodle.
    Tibbs: (spying, appalled) Coats?! Dog-skin coats?!

tropes.name: Wingding Eyes
tropes.html: To go along with Cruella's Nightmare Face during the climactic Chase Scene, especially as she is about to ram the back of the van.

tropes.name: Witch with a Capital "B"
tropes.html: Perdita (who, ironically, is a literal bitch) calls Cruella, "A devil, a-a witch."

tropes.name: Women Drivers
tropes.html: Cruella Drives Like Crazy, and the van driver even cites this trope during the climactic Chase Scene. Justified by Cruella being completely Ax-Crazy.

tropes.name: You Fool!
tropes.html: Like most Disney villains, Cruella loves to call people fools, including Roger and the bumbling henchmen.

tropes.name: You Shall Not Pass!
tropes.html: Captain, Colonel, and Tibbs do this for the Pongos at the old farmhouse, and later the Labrador at Dinsford does it as well — attacking Jasper and Horace so the Dalmatians can escape.

title: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery
original_title: Austin Powers: International Man of Mystery
